arguments.value: 47-year-old man with alcohol use disorder, schizoaffective disorder, ADHD, and depression presented with coffee-ground emesis after heavy drinking. He had hemoglobin drop from 11.0 to 9.5 g/dL and acute kidney injury with creatinine rising from 1.44 mg/dL to 3.01 mg/dL. Endoscopy showed esophagitis and gastritis. He had been taking naltrexone, acamprosate, disulfiram, and gabapentin, along with psychiatric medications, though adherence varied and he reported mixed perceived benefit. During admission, acamprosate and gabapentin were dose-reduced for low GFR and disulfiram was not continued. He later had repeated hospital encounters and was placed on involuntary commitment, after which he remained abstinent for at least six months.
